title: Midnight Neighbor Signal Club
oneLiner: A playful social prototype where solo city dwellers post tiny late-night signals, discover nearby compatible moods, and unlock low-pressure micro-hangouts instead of doomscrolling alone.
targetUser: Urban young adults who feel most isolated late at night and want a safer, lighter way to discover nearby people with matching mood and energy.
keyUX: Send a tiny midnight signal, watch nearby mood matches appear, and unlock a low-pressure shared plan only after both sides opt into the same vibe.
stitchPrompt: Design a bold desktop social concept called Midnight Neighbor Signal Club for urban adults who feel isolated late at night and want something gentler than a full dating app. It should let users post tiny midnight signals, discover nearby people with compatible mood and energy, and unlock low-pressure micro-hangouts only after both sides choose the same vibe. Include a live mood beacon stage, a nearby signal map, a vibe match carousel, a mutual unlock ladder, a micro-hangout suggestion drawer, and a shareable night recap card. Design direction: use a playful-experimental aesthetic with neon night gradients, glossy dark surfaces, luminous map cues, and one clear escalating interaction path so the product feels intimate, stylish, and instantly portfolio-worthy without losing clarity.
